title: The Central Bank's Surplus Transfer Framework
description: Context: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved a monumental, record-breaking surplus transfer of ₹2.87 lakh crore to the Union Government for the financial year 2025–26 (FY26). About The Central Bank’s Surplus Transfer Framework: Key Data and Statistics on RBI’s Financial Performance: The Imperative Need to Deeply Analyze Central Bank Fiscalisation: Key Institutional Challenges and General Criticisms: The RBI’s record-breaking ₹2.87 lakh crore surplus transfer highlights its growing role as a source of state fiscal capacity, moving beyond its traditional mandate as the guardian of monetary stability. While this windfall helps ease federal borrowing pressures, its exclusion from state-level fiscal devolution sharpens structural imbalances within India’s federal framework. Critically evaluate the role being played by RBI in regulating India’s financial sector. (200 Words)

title: The Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement (RELOS)
description: Context: The India-Russia bilateral Logistics Support Agreement (LSA), known as the Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement (RELOA/RELOS), was officially operationalized in January 2026. About The Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement (RELOS): Aim: The aim of RELOS is to simplify and reduce administrative bureaucracy between the two militaries during joint operations. By replacing slow, case-by-case clearances with a standardized accounting system, the agreement aims to accelerate turnaround times, reduce logistics bottlenecks, and extend the operational reach of both nations’ warships and military aircraft.

title: BGP Hijacking
description: Context: Following the Indian government’s temporary block on Telegram, the platform’s founder and CEO Pavel Durov claimed that the app’s global access was being compromised via BGP hijacking.
